A measure that quantifies what it is intended to measure is directly related to the concept of validity, which refers to how well a test or instrument measures what it purports to measure.  
Accuracy generally refers to correctness of measurements in relation to a true value, but not necessarily whether it measures the intended construct.  
Reliability refers to consistency of the measure over time or across items.  
Associative value is not a standard psychometric term in this context.  

Final answer: (B)
